title: Short-circuit gopush when marshaled state is byte-identical
description:
`gopush` (`go/state.go:202`) goes straight from `s.Data()` into `s.data.patcher.patch(newBytes)` with no cheap equality check first. When nothing changed, that still costs a full unmarshal of the whole state into `map[string]any` plus a recursive `objectDiff`, only to produce `{}`.

## Fix

Before calling `patch`, compare `newBytes` against `s.data.bytes`; if equal, skip the patch/diff entirely and leave `version`, `delta` and `patcher.prev` untouched (already correct by construction).

Watch the existing special cases: the `null` clear path, and the `s.data.bytes == nil` → `{}` seeding on first push.

## Sizes

Against the profiled production workload, one push cycle currently processes:

- **341,817 bytes** marshaled out of the state struct
- **341,817 bytes** unmarshaled back into `map[string]any` — 12,189 nodes, **1,585,544 B and 34,014 allocations**
- a recursive diff over 2,502 object nodes and 449 arrays
- to emit a **median 215-byte** delta, or `{}`

Costs, same 341,817-byte payload: full cycle **10.9 ms / 34,942 allocs**, versus `bytes.Equal` at **0.016 ms / 0 allocs** — **678x cheaper**.

## Impact

Measured on the profiled production workload: ~3.7 `gopush`/sec, of which only ~2.1/sec produce a delta, so **~43% of cycles are pure waste** — roughly 4.4 MB/s of pointless decoding.

Smallest change with the highest leverage of the three — a couple of lines. Depends on nothing; do it first.
